hook: Croatia did more of the passing in the final third of the 2018 World Cup Final — and still lost
verified_statistic: Croatia completed 94 of 114 total final-third passes (82.5% field-tilt share) vs France's 20 (17.5%), in a match France won 4-2
plain_english_explanation: Field tilt measures each team's share of completed passes played in the attacking (final) third of the pitch. It is a passing-distribution metric, not a direct measure of territorial control, possession quality, or chance creation.
team_player_match: Croatia vs France, 2018 FIFA World Cup Final, 2018-07-15 (StatsBomb match_id 8658)
comparison_or_baseline: n/a — single-match figure; both teams' full-match completed-pass counts given for context (Croatia 448, France 202)
methodology: locally_calculated. Field tilt = team's completed passes with x>80 (StatsBomb 0-120 pitch, attacking-direction-normalised) / both teams' combined final-third completed passes. metric_id: field_tilt, model_version: event-derived field tilt v1. Reproduced via DuckDB SQL over silver/statsbomb_events (gold/field_tilt_wc2018_final.csv).
confidence: high — simple, fully auditable count over a complete, official event dataset
caveat: Field tilt describes passing distribution, not territory, chance quality, or result. StatsBomb open-data licence requires crediting StatsBomb as source.
suggested_post_copy: Croatia completed 82.5% of the final-third passing in the 2018 World Cup Final. France completed 17.5% — and won 4-2. Field tilt (final-third passing share) isn't the whole story. (Source: StatsBomb Open Data)

hook: Mbappé's World Cup Final volley had a 1-in-10 chance of going in
verified_statistic: Kylian Mbappé's 80th-minute shot (2022 WC Final) carried a StatsBomb xG of 0.102; per StatsBomb's 360 freeze-frame data (the standalone three-sixty product), the nearest opponent captured in the frame was 3.41m away — 8 of Argentina's 11 players on the pitch are captured in this frame
plain_english_explanation: StatsBomb 360 freeze-frame data records the real, tracked positions of players visible around a specific event — here, the instant of the shot. It does not necessarily capture every player on the pitch, so distances describe the nearest CAPTURED opponent, not provably the nearest opponent overall. Opponents are reported anonymously here because StatsBomb's 360 product does not carry player identity.
team_player_match: Kylian Mbappé (France) vs Argentina, 2022 FIFA World Cup Final, 2022-12-18 (StatsBomb match_id 3869685)
comparison_or_baseline: n/a — single-event spatial snapshot; distances given for all 8 captured opposition players (7 outfield + GK) for context
methodology: locally_calculated from provider-supplied positions in StatsBomb's standalone three-sixty file (data/three-sixty/{match}.json, keyed by event_uuid) — this is the canonical StatsBomb 360 product. Distance = Euclidean distance, event-anchored spatial_context, NOT continuous tracking. Reproduced via DuckDB SQL (gold/mbappe_360_wc2022_final.csv).
confidence: high for the distances (direct geometry on official freeze-frame data); StatsBomb's xG model output is itself a modelled estimate, not a measured fact
caveat: RECONCILIATION NOTE (documented, not published as a claim): StatsBomb's event JSON separately embeds a shot.freeze_frame field with named players, giving a different nearest-opponent value (4.05m, Nahuel Molina Lucero) for the same instant — see gold/mbappe_shot_freeze_frame_RECONCILIATION_ONLY.csv. That field is a distinct StatsBomb product ('shot freeze-frame data'), not '360', and is not the source for this claim. Only 8 of Argentina's 11 on-pitch players are captured in the published 360 frame — never say 'nearest defender' as an absolute. StatsBomb attribution required.
suggested_post_copy: 0.10 xG. Per StatsBomb 360, the nearest opponent captured in the freeze-frame was 3.41m away. Mbappé's World Cup Final volley, reconstructed from real tracked positions (8 of 11 Argentina players captured in this frame). (Source: StatsBomb Open Data, 360)

hook: Brisbane Roar's average team width increased by roughly 6m in the second half
verified_statistic: Brisbane Roar's average team width in possession went from 39.22m in the 1st half to 45.35m in the 2nd (81 vs 97 phases with a complete width reading, out of 89 vs 99 total phases); Adelaide United's went from 48.46m to 43.55m (114 vs 112 phases) over the same match
plain_english_explanation: Team width measures how spread out a side is side-to-side while in possession, averaged across each half's possession phases. This describes the measured width numbers directly — it is not a claim about a formation change or tactical intent, which would need positional/formation evidence this dataset doesn't provide.
team_player_match: Brisbane Roar FC 2-3 Adelaide United FC, A-League 2024/25 (2024-11-23, SkillCorner match_id 1874553)
comparison_or_baseline: 1st half vs 2nd half, same match, both teams
methodology: provider_supplied per-phase width fields (team_in_possession_width_start/end), locally_calculated phase-average per half. CANONICAL NULL-HANDLING RULE: a phase contributes to the average only if BOTH width_start and width_end are present (19 of 423 phases match-wide have one missing and are excluded entirely, not repaired from the single present value) — see pipeline/tests/test_team_width_null_handling.py. Reproduced via DuckDB SQL (gold/skillcorner_team_shape.csv); this SQL output is the figure of record.
confidence: medium-high — real per-phase provider fields, reasonable sample (423 phases total), but phase-level not frame-level, and width alone does not establish formation or tactical intent
caveat: Describes this one match's width numbers only; does not imply a formation change or tactical intent. n_phases_used (the complete-pair count) is lower than the match's total phase count because of the null-handling rule above — always report both. SkillCorner licence: MIT.
suggested_post_copy: Brisbane Roar's average team width in possession went from 39.2m in the first half to 45.4m in the second (width data only — not a formation claim). Still lost 2-3. (Source: SkillCorner Open Data)
